transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I can’t sit through long production meetings or edit sessions anymore—I keep getting up and pacing even when I know I should stay in my seat. It has started to cause some issues with my colleagues at work, so I really felt like I needed to seek some help for it.
Can you tell me more about what you experience during these meetings or sessions, such as feeling restless or having difficulty waiting for your turn to speak?

Yes, both of those are huge issues for me. During long meetings, I get this crawling, pent-up energy like I'm in the wrong gear, which drives me to make excuses to get up and pace just to move. I also have a bad habit of cutting people off and blurting out answers or suggestions before they've even finished explaining their point because I get so impatient waiting.
Do you also find it difficult to focus on the details of the discussions or tasks at hand, making careless mistakes or having trouble following through on instructions?

Yes, that is actually a huge problem for me and it's incredibly frustrating. Under tight deadlines, I often skim through briefs too fast and miss obvious things like typos or color notes, which means I have to re-export cuts later. Also, during meetings, I’ll look right at someone but realize my mind has completely drifted off to a shot idea, so I have to ask them to repeat the instructions they just gave me.

Do you often act on impulse without much consideration for the consequences, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or engaging in other impulsive behaviors outside of work, like in your personal relationships or daily activities?

Yes, I definitely do. On set or in meetings, I constantly cut people off and blurt out suggestions before they can even finish explaining their point. I also catch myself jumping into other people's conversations at festivals or offering unsolicited advice on a colleague's work, which makes me feel really pushy and rude afterward.
Can you tell me at what age you first started noticing these symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty with focus and following instructions?

These issues actually go back to my childhood, well before I was 12. In elementary school, my teachers were constantly telling my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat during class. I was always getting up to sharpen my pencil or wandering the room while everyone else worked quietly.

Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity in social or quiet leisure activities, such as reading, watching TV, or engaging in hobbies, outside of work or school settings?

Yes, I definitely struggle with this in my personal life too; my friends actually joke that I never stop. Even on my days off, I constantly bounce from cleaning the apartment to reorganizing hard drives to running errands. If I try to just sit on the couch and relax, I last maybe ten minutes before I feel the urge to get up and do something again.
Do you find it difficult to engage in quiet leisure activities, such as reading a book or watching a movie, without feeling restless or fidgety?

Yes, it’s extremely difficult for me to just sit quietly and relax. If I try to watch a movie or read, I last maybe ten minutes before my legs start bouncing and I feel this crawling, pent-up energy that forces me to get up. I usually end up having to do something active instead, like cleaning the apartment or reorganizing my hard drives.

Can you describe how often you experience physical restlessness, such as fidgeting or feeling the need to move, in situations where you're expected to be still, like when watching a movie or reading a book?

It happens almost constantly whenever I’m expected to be still, whether I'm in a long table read at work or just trying to relax on the couch at home. I constantly fidget by bouncing my legs or drumming my fingers, and I get this crawling, pent-up energy like I'm in the wrong gear. I can barely last ten minutes trying to sit and relax before I feel compelled to get up and do something.
Do you often feel like you're 'on the go' or like you're 'driven by a motor', even when you're not necessarily doing anything physical?

Yes, I absolutely feel that way, like I'm constantly driven by a motor. My friends joke that I never stop because even on my days off, I'm constantly bouncing from task to task like cleaning the apartment or reorganizing hard drives. Trying to just sit on the couch and relax feels impossible—I last maybe ten minutes before I feel that crawling, pent-up energy and have to get up.
Do you experience excessive running, climbing, or other physical activity in situations where it's not appropriate, such as in quiet settings or when you're supposed to be still?

I don't literally run or climb on things as an adult, but I definitely experience the adult equivalent of that. When I have to sit still during a table read or color session, I get an intense, crawling, pent-up physical energy that makes me feel like I'm "in the wrong gear." This internal restlessness is so strong that I constantly have to make excuses to get up and pace the hallways just to release the tension.

Can you describe any instances where you have engaged in excessive physical activity, such as running or climbing, in situations where it was not appropriate, especially during your childhood or adolescence?

I don't really recall doing things like running or climbing in inappropriate places back then. However, I do remember always getting up to wander the classroom or constantly sharpening my pencil instead of staying in my seat during elementary school.
Have you ever been involved in any physically dangerous activities, such as reckless driving or other impulsive behaviors, due to your feelings of restlessness or impulsivity?

No, I haven't really engaged in physically dangerous activities or reckless driving. My impulsivity and restlessness mostly show up in how I communicate with others or my inability to sit still, rather than doing anything physically risky.

Do you feel that your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention are equally problematic in both your work and personal life, or do they tend to cause more issues in one area over the other?

They are definitely much more problematic in my professional life, where my restlessness is actively threatening my career advancement and drawing negative feedback from producers. In contrast, in my personal life, my constant activity is more of a quirk that my friends joke about. While I still find it hard to relax at home, it doesn't cause nearly the same level of distress or impairment as it does at work.

You mentioned that your symptoms are more problematic in your professional life, but can you tell me if you have ever experienced significant distress or impairment in social relationships or other areas of your personal life due to your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention?

Yes, they definitely spill over into my personal and social life. My friends always joke that I can never just sit still and relax, and I can only last about ten minutes on the couch before I have to get up and do something. Also, in social or networking settings, I tend to jump into conversations and interrupt people, which makes me worry that I come off as pushy or rude.

Do you think your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention have caused significant problems in your relationships or daily life, such as straining friendships, causing marital problems, or affecting your ability to maintain a stable living situation?

I haven't really experienced those specific issues, like marital problems or unstable housing. My struggles have been almost entirely concentrated in my professional life and career advancement, while my personal life has remained relatively stable.

Can you estimate the severity of your symptoms, such as restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention, on a scale from 1 to 10, with 1 being mild and 10 being severe, and how have these symptoms impacted your daily life and relationships?

I’d rate my symptoms around a 6 or 7 out of 10, as they significantly impact my career by causing careless editing errors, drifting off during briefings, and pacing in meetings, which is currently holding me back from a senior DP promotion. Socially, my friends constantly joke that I can never just relax, and I often worry that I come off as pushy or rude because I jump into conversations and interrupt people without thinking.

Can you describe how your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention have impacted your daily life and relationships, and do you feel that they are more consistent with a pattern of inattention and disorganization, or with a pattern of hyperactivity and impulsivity?

These symptoms have put a real strain on my career, as my constant pacing has producers questioning my readiness for a senior promotion, while my friends notice I can never relax and my interrupting makes me feel pushy. While I do have moments where I drift off or skim over details, my daily struggles are overwhelmingly tied to physical restlessness, an inability to stay seated, and impulsivity. Because of that, I definitely feel my issues are much more consistent with a pattern of hyperactivity and impulsivity.

Can you clarify if you experience more distress or impairment from your symptoms of hyperactivity, such as restlessness and impulsivity, or from symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty focusing or following through on instructions?

While I definitely have some attention issues like drifting off or making detail errors, the hyperactivity and physical restlessness cause me far more distress and impairment. It's my inability to stay in my seat and constant pacing during meetings that led to a producer warning me about my behavior. That physical restlessness is what is actively threatening my promotion to a senior DP role.
Have you ever experienced any periods in your life where your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity significantly improved or disappeared for a while, only to return later?

I don't recall any period in my life where these symptoms of restlessness and hyperactivity completely disappeared or significantly improved. However, they were definitely less noticeable and much easier to manage when my work was more active and solo, before my job role shifted over the last couple of years.

Can you estimate the relative frequency of days where you experience significant hyperactivity symptoms, such as restlessness and impulsivity, compared to days where you experience significant inattention symptoms, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions?

I haven't really tracked it in terms of specific days or percentages, so I'm not sure of the exact ratio. However, both feel quite frequent, with the physical restlessness and need to move being a constant daily struggle for me.

Do you think your difficulties with focus and following instructions are primarily due to your inability to sit still and constant need to move, or do you feel that they are separate issues that also cause you significant distress?

They are deeply connected, because forcing myself to sit still and manage that pent-up, restless energy takes so much conscious effort that I have little mental bandwidth left to actually process what is being said. That said, I do also experience separate focus issues, like my mind drifting off to creative shot ideas during meetings or rushing and skimming past important written details on briefs.

Do you think your symptoms of hyperactivity, such as restlessness and impulsivity, or your symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions, are more prominent and cause you more distress in your daily life?

While I definitely have trouble focusing, like drifting off or skimming past details, the hyperactivity and physical restlessness are much more prominent and cause me the most distress. My inability to stay seated, constant pacing, and blurting out answers are what actually drove me to seek help, as they are directly harming my professional reputation and holding me back from a promotion.

Do you feel that your hyperactive symptoms, such as restlessness and impulsivity, or your inattentive symptoms, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions, have been more persistent and problematic throughout your life?

The hyperactive and restless symptoms have definitely been far more persistent and problematic throughout my life. While I do sometimes drift off or make detail errors, my inability to sit still and constant need to move have been a struggle since elementary school, when my teachers complained about me constantly wandering the classroom.
Can you describe a typical day, from waking up to bedtime, and how your symptoms of restlessness, impulsivity, and inattention affect your daily activities and interactions?

In morning production meetings, I struggle to stay in my seat, drift off mentally, and constantly blurt out suggestions before others finish. During afternoon editing, I fidget constantly, interrupt my colleagues, and make careless errors like missing color notes because I skimmed the brief too quickly. Evenings at home are no different; I can't just sit on the couch and relax, so I end up pacing, cleaning, or reorganizing my hard drives.

Do you think your symptoms of hyperactivity, such as restlessness and impulsivity, are more closely tied to situations where you are required to be still and quiet, or do they occur more frequently in situations where you are allowed to be more active?

They are definitely much more intense and problematic in situations where I'm required to be still and quiet, like during long production meetings or when trying to relax on the couch. In those quiet moments, I feel a crawling, pent-up energy that forces me to fidget or find excuses to get up. While I'm still constantly on the go when I'm allowed to be active, it feels much more manageable when I can actually move.

Can you estimate the proportion of your daily struggles that are due to difficulties with hyperactivity and impulsivity, such as restlessness and interrupting, versus difficulties with inattention, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions?

I'm not really sure of the exact proportion, as I haven't ever thought about my struggles in terms of percentages. While I definitely experience both, the physical restlessness and my absolute inability to stay seated feel like the most constant and disruptive issues in my daily life.

Do you think your symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity are primarily driven by an inability to control your physical movements and verbal responses, or are they more related to difficulties with sustained attention and organization?

I would say they are primarily driven by an inability to control my physical movements and verbal impulses. While I certainly struggle with drifting off and missing details, it's the intense physical urge to get up and pace, and the sudden drive to blurt out answers, that feel the most dominant and hardest to suppress.

Can you compare the level of distress or impairment you experience due to your hyperactive symptoms, such as restlessness and impulsivity, versus your inattentive symptoms, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions, and tell me which one currently causes you more problems in your daily life?

While both cause issues, my hyperactive and restless symptoms definitely cause significantly more distress and impairment in my daily work life. Although I do sometimes struggle with focus, like drifting off in meetings or skimming details in emails, it is my physical restlessness and leaving my seat during important production meetings that has drawn direct criticism from producers. That physical restlessness is what is actively threatening my career advancement to a senior DP role.

Do you think your difficulties with hyperactivity, such as restlessness and impulsivity, or your difficulties with inattention, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions, are more central to your overall experience and daily struggles?

While both definitely play a role, the hyperactivity and physical restlessness are much more central to my daily struggles. Although I do sometimes drift off or miss small details, it is the constant, pent-up physical energy and my struggle to stay seated during meetings that cause me the most distress and are actively jeopardizing my career advancement.

Do you think your symptoms of hyperactivity, such as restlessness and impulsivity, are more closely tied to your difficulties with inattention, such as difficulty focusing or following instructions, or do they seem to be distinct issues that affect you in different ways?

I'm not entirely sure, and I haven't really thought about whether they are directly connected. Both the physical restlessness and the mental drifting feel like different, challenging aspects that disrupt my work in their own distinct ways.
